question: Your team built two workflows for the support agent. The quality review checks every resolved refund ticket each week for the same five aspects, but it uses dynamic decomposition, and each weekly report covers a different mix of aspects. The takeover investigation uses a fixed prompt chain of get_customer, then lookup_order, then escalate_to_human, and it misses linked accounts that surface midway through a case. Which causes explain these two problems?

options.text: Both problems come from a context window that is too small, so the agent loses track of earlier aspects and leads regardless of the decomposition pattern each workflow uses.
options.reason: The symptoms match a pattern mismatch that the guide describes: the review needs prompt chaining and the investigation needs dynamic decomposition. A larger context fixes neither.

options.text: The quality review covers too many aspects for any automated decomposition, so its reports will vary until human reviewers check every resolved ticket by hand.
options.reason: The guide says prompt chaining handles predictable multi-aspect reviews with one focused pass per aspect, so the number of aspects is not the cause.

options.text: The quality review is a predictable multi-aspect review, but dynamic decomposition lets the agent choose different subtasks on each run, so some aspects get skipped.
options.reason: The guide matches predictable multi-aspect reviews to prompt chaining, where the same focused passes run every time. Dynamic decomposition here causes the varying coverage.

options.text: The takeover investigation is open-ended, but its fixed chain cannot generate new subtasks from intermediate findings, so a linked account found midway is never examined.
options.reason: The guide matches open-ended investigations to dynamic decomposition, which generates subtasks from what each step discovers. A fixed chain cannot follow new leads.

options.text: The takeover investigation chain is simply too short, so running the same fixed order with extra lookup_order steps for every case would catch each linked account.
options.reason: More fixed steps still cannot react to what a case reveals. The guide says open-ended investigations need subtasks generated from intermediate findings.
